title: Grade 4 Science — Thu, Jun 19
description: Skeletal System — Day 4 of 5: Muscular system — muscles, tendons, voluntary vs involuntary
subject: science

questions.question: The muscular system works together with the skeletal system to:
questions.explanation: Muscles attach to bones and pull on them when they contract (shorten). This is how the body moves.

questions.question: The human body has approximately how many muscles?
questions.explanation: The human body has over 600 muscles! They make up about 40% of body weight.

questions.question: VOLUNTARY muscles are muscles that:
options: Can be controlled consciously (we decide when to use them)
Are found only in the heart
questions.explanation: Voluntary muscles are under conscious control. We decide to move them — like lifting an arm or walking.

questions.question: Which is an example of a VOLUNTARY muscle?
questions.explanation: The bicep (arm muscle) is voluntary — you consciously decide to lift your arm. Heart and stomach muscles are involuntary.

questions.question: INVOLUNTARY muscles are muscles that:
options: Are found only in arms and legs
questions.explanation: Involuntary muscles work automatically — we do not control them consciously. Examples: heart, stomach, intestines.

questions.question: Which is an example of an INVOLUNTARY muscle?
options: Stomach muscle that churns food during digestion
Eye muscle when we blink voluntarily
questions.explanation: Stomach muscles work involuntarily — they churn food automatically during digestion without us thinking about it.

questions.question: The heart is made of a special type of muscle called:
questions.explanation: The heart is made of cardiac muscle — a special type found only in the heart. It beats automatically without stopping.

questions.question: Smooth muscle is found in:
options: The walls of internal organs like the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle lines the walls of internal organs (stomach, intestines, blood vessels). It works involuntarily to move food, blood, etc.

questions.question: Skeletal muscle (striated muscle) is:
options: Attached to bones — voluntary and controls body movement
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle attaches to bones and is under voluntary control. It is the main type of muscle that moves our limbs.

questions.question: Tendons are:
options: Tough bands connecting bone to bone
Strong cords connecting muscle to bone
questions.explanation: Tendons are strong, cord-like connective tissues that connect muscles to bones. When muscles contract, tendons pull the bones to create movement.

questions.question: What is the difference between a tendon and a ligament?
options: Tendon = muscle to bone; Ligament = bone to bone
Tendon = bone to bone; Ligament = muscle to bone
Tendons are in the heart; ligaments are in the legs
questions.explanation: Tendon: connects MUSCLE to BONE. Ligament: connects BONE to BONE. Easy memory: Ten-don → muscle to bone (ten-don).

questions.question: When a muscle contracts (shortens), it:
options: Pulls the bone towards it, causing movement
questions.explanation: Muscles only PULL — they cannot push. When a bicep contracts, it pulls the forearm up towards the shoulder.

questions.question: Muscles work in pairs. When the bicep contracts (lifts the forearm), the tricep must:
questions.explanation: Muscles work in antagonistic pairs. When the bicep contracts, the tricep relaxes. When the tricep contracts (to straighten the arm), the bicep relaxes.

questions.question: Exercise makes muscles:
questions.explanation: Regular exercise causes muscle fibres to grow thicker and stronger. This is why athletes have larger, stronger muscles than sedentary people.

questions.question: Which of the three muscle types is found ONLY in the heart?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is unique to the heart. It beats continuously without rest for an entire lifetime — involuntary, striated, and never tires.
